 MCCAYSVILLE, Ga. — McCaysville’s water system remains out of operation, and officials say they cannot estimate when service will be restored.
 Heavy flooding inundated downtown McCaysville, Georgia, and Copperhill, Tennessee, Thursday after overnight rain sent water through streets and over bridges. Video from the area showed deep water covering roads and bridges.
 Michael Earley Fixed vo₀₋₁₀₈ 
 McCaysville Police Chief Michael Earley said the city was closed to unauthorized personnel until further notice, limiting access to emergency and safety workers. Blue Ridge Drive at the bridge and the Steel Bridge were also closed because of active flooding.
 The Tennessee Valley Authority said Thursday morning that a flood-control operation in Ocoee had been holding back water in Blue Ridge since Nov. 3. Water was spilling from Ocoee 3 Dam in Copperhill at a rate of 150,000 gallons per second. TVA urged people to stay away from the fast-moving river.
 TVA's Scott Fiedler discuss flooding in McCaysville on ARC Chattanooga (VIDEO: WTVC) 
 Business owners said damage to buildings, businesses, property and infrastructure will require a coordinated recovery effort.
 “I think when it comes to the destruction of items and products and buildings and real estate, I think that’s gonna be the big issue down there and it’s gonna take a lot of people coming together to try to remediate the situation,” said Jodie Nicholson, a Copperhill business owner. Heavy flooding in Copperhill, Tenn. (PHOTO WTVC) 
 A Copperhill business owner identified as Double Whammy said the flooding was worse than a previous event, when the river did not overflow its banks. This time, the river rose over its banks, while additional water flowed down Harper Town Hill into McCaysville.
 The Ocoee Country Chamber of Commerce is coordinating donations and supplies for emergency responders and families displaced by the flooding. Needed items include prepared meals, diapers, wipes, bottles, formula and toiletries. Monetary donations are being accepted at the chamber’s office in Benton and the Jackie Rogers County Clerk’s office.
 Heavy flooding in Copperhill, Tenn. (PHOTO WTVC) 
 Food is available for people in need at Luttrell’s Hardware in Copperhill. Emergency workers can get meals at Rod’s Rockin’ Rolls in Ducktown and the Copperhill Sahara Club.
 A popular pull-off along the Ocoee River, usually filled with parked cars, was underwater Thursday.
 US Representative Clay Fuller says he's keeping a close eye on the situation in Murray County as first responders work into the night.
 "I am closely monitoring the flooding impacting Murray County and surrounding areas of NW Georgia. My team stands ready to help in every way. My thoughts and prayers are with everyone affected, and I am grateful to the first responders and emergency personnel working to keep Georgians safe." Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp has declared a state of emergency for Fannin, Gilmer, Murray and Union County.
 Swiftwater teams sent to Fannin County 
 The Mowbray Volunteer Fire Department said its Swiftwater rescue team was dispatched to Fannin County early Thursday to assist with flash flooding and mudslides.
 The Tri-State Mutual Aid Swiftwater response included Cleveland Fire; Bradley County Fire Rescue and EMS B-SORT; McMinn County Fire; Fannin County Fire; Hiwassee Dam Fire; Dallas Bay Volunteer Fire Department; STARS; East Ridge Fire; the Hamilton County OEM Drone Team; Wolf Creek Fire; Etowah Fire; Englewood Fire; Athens Fire; Mowbray Volunteer Fire Department; Chattanooga Fire; Copper Basin Fire; West Polk County Fire; and the Rhea County Fire Drone Team.
 Crews rescuing a man near Bridge Street in Copperhill. The city is currently closed due to overnight floods. 
 The response also included Mutual Aid Chiefs Dewey Woody, Mike Williams, Billy Roach and Jeff Stewart.
 McCaysville plans water distribution 
 The City of McCaysville said its water system remains out of operation because of the flooding and that it cannot estimate when water service will be fully restored. The city said restoration could take a lengthy period and asked residents to conserve water and follow the boil water advisory in effect.
 The city plans to distribute water to customers served by the McCaysville water system from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Friday, Nov. 6, at the building behind McCaysville City Hall.
 Floodwaters are receding along the Tennessee-Georgia state line, revealing the damage left behind by devastating flooding overnight Nov. 5. (PHOTO WTVC) 
 City officials said employees and public safety personnel are working to assist residents and restore essential services. They also acknowledged the hardship the flooding has caused residents, businesses and families and asked the community to remain patient.
